Assumed all three sides are equal without noticing the base $AB=6$ differs from the two slant sides of $5$.
Treated the opposite signs of $m_{AC}=\tfrac43$ and $m_{BC}=-\tfrac43$ as enough for perpendicular sides, without checking that their product is $-\tfrac{16}{9}$, not $-1$.
Read the right angle at $P$ without checking that $m_{PQ}\times m_{PR}$ is not $-1$.

questions.solution_text:
$m_{PQ}=\dfrac{2-(-2)}{1-(-1)}$
$=2$
$m_{QR}=\dfrac{0-2}{5-1}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{2}$
$m_{PQ}\times m_{QR}=2\times\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$
$=-1$
$PQ\perp QR$, so the right angle is at $Q$.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{midpoint }EG=\left(\dfrac{-2+4}{2},\dfrac{-1+1}{2}\right)$
$=(1,0)$
$\text{midpoint }FH=\left(\dfrac{2+0}{2},\dfrac{-2+2}{2}\right)$
$=(1,0)$
The diagonals share the midpoint $(1,0)$, so they bisect each other and $EFGH$ is a parallelogram.

options.why: Read four equal sides as enough for a square, but the angles are not right angles here.
Stopped at opposite sides equal, a weaker property than all four sides being equal.
Equal sides do not make a rectangle, which instead needs a right angle.

questions.solution_text:
$AB=\sqrt{(2-(-1))^2+(1-(-3))^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5$
$BC=\sqrt{(-1-2)^2+(5-1)^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5$
$CD=\sqrt{(-4-(-1))^2+(1-5)^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5$
$DA=\sqrt{(-1-(-4))^2+(-3-1)^2}=\sqrt{9+16}=5$
All four sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is a rhombus.
$AC=\sqrt{(-1-(-1))^2+(5-(-3))^2}=8$
$BD=\sqrt{(-4-2)^2+(1-1)^2}=6$
The diagonals are unequal, so this rhombus is not a square. Its most precise name is rhombus.

options.why: Equal opposite gradients give parallel sides, but a rectangle also needs adjacent sides to be perpendicular.
Treated only one pair of sides as parallel, when both pairs are parallel here.
Parallel opposite sides do not force the four sides to be equal in length, which a rhombus requires.

$=-\dfrac{1}{4}$
$m_{DC}=\dfrac{1-2}{3-(-1)}$
$=-\dfrac{1}{4}$
$m_{BC}=\dfrac{1-(-3)}{3-1}$
$=2$
$m_{AD}=\dfrac{2-(-2)}{-1-(-3)}$
$=2$
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel, so $ABCD$ is a parallelogram.
$m_{AB}\times m_{BC}=-\dfrac14\times2=-\dfrac12$, which is not $-1$, so it is not a rectangle.
$AB=\sqrt{(1-(-3))^2+(-3-(-2))^2}=\sqrt{17}$
$BC=\sqrt{(3-1)^2+(1-(-3))^2}=\sqrt{20}$
The adjacent sides are unequal, so it is not a rhombus. Its most precise name is parallelogram.

questions.solution_text:
$AC=\sqrt{(5-(-2))^2+(5-1)^2}=\sqrt{49+16}=\sqrt{65}$
$BD=\sqrt{(1-2)^2+(7-(-1))^2}=\sqrt{1+64}=\sqrt{65}$
$\text{midpoint }AC=\left(\dfrac{-2+5}{2},\dfrac{1+5}{2}\right)=\left(\dfrac32,3\right)$
$\text{midpoint }BD=\left(\dfrac{2+1}{2},\dfrac{-1+7}{2}\right)=\left(\dfrac32,3\right)$
$m_{AC}=\dfrac{5-1}{5-(-2)}=\dfrac47$
$m_{BD}=\dfrac{7-(-1)}{1-2}=-8$
$m_{AC}\times m_{BD}=-\dfrac{32}{7}$, which is not $-1$.
The diagonals are equal and bisect each other, so $ABCD$ is a rectangle. They are not perpendicular, so it is not a square or a rhombus; its most precise name is rectangle.

options.why: Four equal sides give a rhombus, but the equal diagonals also force right angles, making it a square.
Equal diagonals suggest a rectangle, but here the four sides are also equal, which a rectangle need not have.
Named only the weakest property, when equal sides and equal diagonals give a far more specific shape.

questions.solution_text:
$AB=\sqrt{(-1-2)^2+(2-1)^2}=\sqrt{9+1}=\sqrt{10}$
$BC=\sqrt{(-2-(-1))^2+(-1-2)^2}=\sqrt{1+9}=\sqrt{10}$
$CD=\sqrt{(1-(-2))^2+(-2-(-1))^2}=\sqrt{9+1}=\sqrt{10}$
$DA=\sqrt{(2-1)^2+(1-(-2))^2}=\sqrt{1+9}=\sqrt{10}$
All four sides are equal, so $ABCD$ is a rhombus.
$AC=\sqrt{(-2-2)^2+(-1-1)^2}$
$=\sqrt{20}$
$BD=\sqrt{(1-(-1))^2+(-2-2)^2}$
$=\sqrt{20}$
The diagonals are equal, so the rhombus has right angles.
A rhombus with equal diagonals is a square, so $ABCD$ is a square.
